page: Amazon Web Services m7gd.2xlarge is a general-purpose cloud instance built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor. It runs on an ARM64 architecture powered by eight physical AWS Neoverse-V1 cores clocked at 2.6 GHz, offering dedicated vCPU execution without multi-threading. The instance includes 32.0 GB of system RAM, maintaining a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio of 4.0 GB per core. Hardware specifications feature 474 GB of local NVMe SSD instance storage for low-latency ephemeral disk operations, hardware-accelerated AES cryptography, and a baseline network bandwidth of 4 Gbps.

In benchmark evaluations, the m7gd.2xlarge demonstrates strong memory subsystem performance, scoring in the top 25th percentile for memory bandwidth. General compute workloads produce consistent mid-tier results, including stress-ng multi-core execution, Geekbench software compilation, static web serving at 15.88 GB/sec, and Redis SET throughput reaching 13.58 million operations per second. However, heavy instruction decompression like bzip3 and medium LLM prompt processing exhibit weaker performance due to the underlying ARM core architecture and absence of x86 vector extensions.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, bundling dedicated local NVMe storage directly with ARM-based Graviton compute delivers high resource density without requiring separate block storage attachments. The instance provides strong performance per resource for memory-bound and storage-intensive tasks. Best-fit workloads for the m7gd.2xlarge include relational databases, key-value stores, software build nodes, static web servers, and intermediate data processing jobs.
description: Amazon Web Services m7gd.2xlarge is a general-purpose cloud instance powered by eight dedicated ARM64 AWS Neoverse-V1 cores running at 2.6 GHz on the Nitro hypervisor. It provides 32.0 GB of RAM alongside 474 GB of integrated local NVMe SSD storage and 4 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. Memory subsystem performance is strong, landing in the top quartile of benchmark tests, while standard CPU operations, Redis SET throughput (13.58 million ops/sec), static web serving (15.88 GB/sec), and general software compilation achieve solid mid-tier performance. Specialized operations such as bzip3 decompression and instruction-heavy encryption perform lower due to ARM architectural constraints. By pairing efficient Graviton compute cores with fast local instance storage, the m7gd.2xlarge offers qualitative cost efficiency for workloads that demand balanced vCPU-to-RAM ratios and fast ephemeral storage. It is suitable for database instances, web applications, software builds, and ETL pipelines.
